idiom_name: thin typed DOM listener + pure typed module (Vitest, Testing Library queries)
implementation_notes: The framework-free realization in TypeScript: the listener reads from the event target, calls a typed module function and writes back, so the DOM edge is tiny and the logic module is tested with Vitest without a DOM (a DOM environment is only needed when the shell itself is exercised). Types replace the classic structure: narrow parameters and a discriminated result make the boundary explicit, and Testing Library queries by role or label keep DOM tests from pinning markup. Choose the plain module when the page is not component-based; otherwise the React variant is the framework-shaped form of the same split.
pitfalls: Handler creep: the listener accumulates parsing, fallbacks and calculations; keep it read-call-write so the typed module stays the only place where decisions live.
Casting DOM values (dataset entries are string | undefined) inside the logic module re-imports the DOM; parse at the edge and keep the module's input types honest.
Vitest's default node environment has no DOM, so shell tests must opt into a DOM environment explicitly or they fail on document.

variants.name: React function component + typed custom hook or reducer
variants.idiom_name: pure typed function component + custom hook / reducer holding the logic
variants.implementation_notes: The declarative realization: keep components pure (React may call them twice in strict mode) and move state and calculations into a typed custom hook or reducer that Vitest calls directly, so rendering is a pure mapping from props and state to JSX. Requires React with hooks (16.8+) plus the React type definitions; choose it when the screen is React, and the DOM-module variant when it is not.
pitfalls: Strict Mode double-invokes components in development, so impure render code misbehaves exactly where purity was ignored; the framework is detecting the violation the pattern prevents.
Logic left in the component body (derived values, subscriptions) cannot be driven from a test without rendering; move it into the hook or reducer.
